Jaimini
------------------------------------------
A well-known sage, जैमिनि was one of the four chief disciples of व्यास or वेदव्यास. He is said to have had a thorough एदुचतिओन् in the Sāmaveda.
He was the author of the Pūrva-mīmāṁsā-sūtras and the Nyāyamālā-vistara. Other works attributed to him are: Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa, Jaiminīya Gṛhyasūtra and Jaiminīya Śrautasūtra.
Born in the lineage of another great sage Kutsa, he was the उद्गातृ (priest of the Sāmaveda) in the सर्पयाग or serpent sacrifice conducted by जनमेजय, the great-grandson of अर्जुन.
He was a champion of the Vedic sacrificial religion.
Another sage, Talavakāra, credited with the revelation of the Talavakāra Upaniṣad (also known as Kenopaniṣad), was his disciple.

Jaimini-sūtras
------------------------------------------
The Pūrvamīmāṁsā-sūtras of जैमिनि is sometimes called Jaimini-sūtras.
See PŪRVAMĪMĀṀSĀ-DARŚANA.

Jaiminīya Gṛhyasūtras
------------------------------------------
Jaimini was the third of the four chief disciples of व्यास, also known as वेदव्यास. It was to him that the Sāmaveda was taught.
One of the works attributed to him is the Jaiminīya Gṛhyasūtras. It has two khaṇḍas or sections. The first has 24 kaṇḍikās (prose mantras) and the second 9. There is a commentary by one श्रीनिवास Adhvarin.
Subjects generally described in the गृह्यसूत्रस् like the ṣoḍaśa or the sixteen सṁस्कारस् (sacraments) are dealt with here also.
